title: Stanley Robillard inquest hears how man failed by system
subtitle: Saskatoon emergency services changed in wake of 2010 death
article: Stanley Robillard waited in the St. Paul's Hospital emergency room for 90 minutes with a serious head injury, his inquest heard today.
Robillard, 46, died in police custody on July 15, 2010. He had been arrested for public intoxication. He was taken to the police station after waiting at the hospital.
He had suffered a serious head injury after falling in a parking lot.
Dr. James Stempien is the head of emergency services for the Saskatoon Health Region. He oversees St. Paul's, City and Royal University hospitals.
"This was a failure of the system in general," he said today at Robillard's inquest.
The health region did a sweeping review of emergency room practices after Robillard's death, and made big changes, he said.
"The national standards haven't changed. We changed," he said.

One of the key changes is setting time limits on how long patients wait in emergency before seeing a doctor. Stempien said the aim now is to have patient-doctor interaction within 30 minutes, "so they're no longer waiting on stretchers in hallways."
Staff now use an electronic system to help assess the severity of injuries. Patients are scored on a scale of one to five, and this helps with the patient flow in busy times.
"Triage is not a perfect skill, there is still some human interaction," Stempien said.
"This helps create the same playing field."
And, doctors are now informed when a waiting patient decides to check out of emergency. A doctor can now decide to see that patient more quickly.
